questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I chose to go on exchange to Monash University in Melbourne because it has a strong reputation for law and offers a different perspective on legal studies. I wanted to learn more about how the legal system works in Australia and compare it to what I’ve studied at home.

Melbourne is also a diverse and exciting city, which made it a great place to experience a new culture while continuing my studies. Monash has a welcoming environment for international students, and I knew I would gain both academic knowledge and personal growth from the experience

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The orientation at Monash University was well-organized and really helpful. It was easy to find the information I needed when I arrived. The staff and student volunteers were friendly and gave clear guidance on things like enrolling in classes, using campus facilities, and settling into life in Melbourne. The welcome sessions and tours made it easier to understand how everything worked, and there were plenty of resources available online as well. Overall, the support made the transition smooth and stress-free.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I arrived at Monash University, I received helpful assistance through their orientation program. Staff and student volunteers were available to answer questions, help with directions, and explain how to set up things like student accounts, transport cards, and class registration. There were also welcome events and tours that made it easier to meet people and get familiar with the campus. Overall, the support made settling in much easier.

Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It wasn’t too easy to find off-campus housing before arriving, so I booked an Airbnb for the first couple of weeks and started looking once I got there. That made it easier to visit places in person and choose something that suited me. I recommend doing the same—book temporary accommodation first, then look around once you're in Melbourne. Websites like
Flatmates.com.au
were helpful, and it’s good to check student Facebook groups too.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Future exchange students should know that living off campus gives you more independence and a chance to explore different parts of Melbourne, but it also means you need to manage things like rent, bills, and transport. Make sure the place you choose is close to public transport so it’s easy to get to campus. Start looking early, be prepared for competition, and always inspect the place in person before signing anything. It’s also a good idea to have some temporary accommodation booked for when you first arrive.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process at Monash University started before arrival, with emails explaining how to set up my student account and choose classes online. Once I arrived, the orientation week helped guide me through the final steps. I attended welcome sessions, confirmed my enrolment, and received my student ID. Staff and student volunteers were available to help with any issues, and most tasks could be done online through the Monash student portal. The process was smooth and well-organized.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Monash University offered a lot of help for exchange students. During orientation, there were staff and student volunteers available to answer questions and guide us through things like enrolment, using campus facilities, and public transport. There were also information sessions, campus tours, and help desks. If you needed more support, you could book appointments with student services or ask for help at the international student office. Everyone was friendly and willing to help, which made settling in much easier.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Registering for the classes I wanted was a bit challenging. It was difficult to organize my schedule so that the classes didn’t overlap, and the process was a little confusing at times. The course system and timetable were different from what I was used to, which made it harder to plan. However, with some patience and help from the staff, I was able to finalize my schedule in the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My advice for future exchange students is to start planning your classes early and double-check your timetable to avoid overlapping. Don’t be afraid to ask for help from staff if you’re confused—they’re there to support you. Take your time to understand the system, and be flexible with your choices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses at Monash University was adequate for my studies. They were challenging enough to help me learn and grow, but not too difficult to manage. The content matched what I expected and fit well with my background in law. Overall, the courses provided a good balance between theory and practical skills.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at Monash University was much more interactive compared to UCPH. There was a stronger focus on class discussions, group work, and practical examples, which made learning more engaging. At Monash, students were encouraged to actively participate and share their opinions, which was different from the more lecture-based approach I’m used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Australian legal process and research - 6 credit points
Indigenous peoples and the law - 6 credit points
International Criminal Justice - 6 credit points
Arbitration of International Commercial Disputes - 6 credit points

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the course Australian Legal Process and Research to future exchange students. It provides a great introduction to how the Australian legal system works and teaches important research skills that are useful for studying law anywhere. The course is practical and helps you understand the differences between legal systems, which is really valuable for anyone interested in comparative law.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Some unexpected costs I encountered included public transport fares, which added up more than I expected. I also had extra expenses for social activities and food when eating out. It’s a good idea to budget a bit extra for these kinds of costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out in Melbourne was a bit more expensive than I expected. Compared to my home country, meals at cafes and restaurants cost more, especially in popular areas near campus. However, groceries and public transport were about what I expected. It’s a good idea to cook at home often to save money.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Monash University offered a wide range of cultural, athletic, and social activities for students. There were clubs and societies for different interests, including cultural groups where you could meet people from around the world. The university also had sports teams and fitness classes for staying active. Social events like welcome parties, movie nights, and workshops helped exchange students connect and make friends. Overall, there were plenty of opportunities to get involved and enjoy campus life.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend future exchange students join clubs or groups to meet new people and learn about different cultures. Doing sports or exercise is also good to stay healthy and have fun. Plus, exploring Melbourne by going to festivals, markets, or parks is a great way to enjoy your time here. These activities help you make friends and have a better experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend visiting students explore some of Melbourne’s famous spots like Federation Square, the Royal Botanic Gardens, and St Kilda Beach. Taking a trip along the Great Ocean Road to see the Twelve Apostles is also amazing if you have more time. On weekends, checking out local markets, cafes, and live music events is a fun way to experience the city’s culture. These activities help you enjoy Melbourne and make the most of your free time.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the local culture in Melbourne was easy. People were friendly and welcoming, and I quickly got used to the lifestyle and customs. Being in a diverse city with many international students also made it easier to feel at home. Overall, I felt comfortable adapting to the new environment.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I don’t have any specific tips for socializing with local students, but I found that being open and friendly helps a lot. Joining campus activities or clubs can also be a good way to meet people naturally.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: One cultural difference I found challenging was getting used to the big city environment and seeing a lot of homeless people around. It was different from what I was used to, and it took some time to understand and accept this part of life in Melbourne.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated how friendly and open people in Melbourne are. The city is very multicultural, so it was great to meet people from all over the world and learn about different cultures. I also liked the relaxed lifestyle and the strong focus on work-life balance.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Book temporary accommodation like an Airbnb before you arrive, so you have a place to stay while you look for longer-term housing.

Start planning your course registration early and ask for help if you find the process confusing.

Get involved in clubs and social activities to meet new people and make the most of your time in Melbourne.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don’t have any other information to add, but I’m happy to share more if needed.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was getting to learn about a new legal system and culture while meeting people from all over the world. It helped me grow both academically and personally, and gave me memories and skills that I will carry with me for life

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during my exchange was adjusting to the different teaching style and managing my class schedule without overlaps. It was a bit confusing at first, but with time and help from staff, I was able to handle it.

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
